entries.subject: DAMIT 185: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-185.txt. Model 185, version 2007-02-27, pole (74°, 27°), period 23.9845 h match the retained metadata. The archive diameter field is 115 ±12 km; its applicability to our scale is a separate calibration decision. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: Torppa et al. (2003), Shapes and rotational properties of thirty asteroids from photometric data
entries.finding: [Torppa et al. (2003), Shapes and rotational properties of thirty asteroids from photometric data](https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2003Icar..164..346T) — original model publication record.

entries.subject: AKARI thermal diameter as an alternative scale
entries.finding: [AKARI AcuA](https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/akari/AKARI-IRC_Catalogue_AllSky_AcuA_1.0/) — retained for comparison; the documented physical calibration supplies the selected scale. Its fitted nonrotating-sphere diameter is 108.28 ± 1.18 km. Formal catalog error omits additional shape, spin and thermal-model effects; no total confidence interval is invented. The original catalogue row for asteroid 230 was retrieved again and matched field-for-field with the retained row, including diameter, reported error and detection count.
entries.revisitWhen: A source-specific comparison with the selected shape and physical calibration justifies changing the adopted scale.

entries.subject: Hanuš et al. (2013), Icarus 226, 1045–1057
entries.finding: [Hanuš et al. (2013), Icarus 226, 1045–1057](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1308.0446) — retained primary publication; see the body-specific selection and calibration above.

entries.subject: Registered surface imagery
entries.finding: Included 2026-09-18 as the SPHERE photograph lens: 14 camera-1 deconvolved frames, 2018-09-26 and 2018-09-28, cast onto the ADAM mesh with cameras computed from the release rotation record, JPL Horizons and each frame’s header. Its registration is the published comparison recorded in zimpol-published-comparison. Earlier finding, kept: The release supplies no registered surface imagery; the grid marks that gap.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: Alternative archive solutions: model 186, pole ['237', '29'], [Model 186](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroid_models/view/186) The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 186: pole (237°, 29°), 23.9845 h, version 2007-02-27, archive diameter 116 km. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.

entries.subject: VLT/SPHERE/ZIMPOL deconvolved frames as a computed-camera photograph lens
entries.finding: Decided 2026-09-18 by the published comparison instead: the lens is prepared from 14 camera-1 frames on the ADAM mesh with the rotation record read latitude-first, and ships on zimpol-published-comparison; the registration stage’s numbers are in the README. Earlier result, kept: Measured with the cross-frame registration test on 14 deconvolved ZIMPOL frames (camera 1), each held against a reference built from the body's frames more than an hour away, cast through the ADAM reconstruction with the survey's rotation record read latitude-first. Disc interior 254 pixels (median); peak correlation 0.30 (median) against a mirror margin of 0.66; 0 of 14 frames decisive by the stated rule (peak at least 0.15 and margin at least 1.5), of which 0 peak within 5 degrees of the model. The frames carry no markings the test can register, so nothing in them confirms or refutes the rotation record's phase, pole or handedness; the silhouette gate that qualified Kleopatra cannot judge a body this round either. A photograph lens for this body would rest on the survey's record read by the route proven on Vesta and on five elongated bodies, with no check on this body itself; it is not derived until one exists.

entries.subject: Vernazza et al. (2021) Figure B.38 as the registration of the SPHERE photograph lens
entries.finding: Measured with tools/objects/sphere-survey/setup.mts against Vernazza et al. (2021) Figure B.38, the survey’s comparison of these frames with its models. Outline overlap with the paper’s ADAM panels 0.925 to 0.954 at our phase, against 0.951 to 0.955 for our own outline drawn at the paper’s pixel scale; over a full turn in 10° steps it peaks at our phase in 2 of 3 columns, one step from it in 1. With the paper’s photographs 0.906 to 0.936. Turned in the image, our outline best overlaps the paper’s photographs at -5.5 to 0.0° and its model panels at -1.5 to 1.0°. The spin axis we project lies at 84.6° on the sky against 112.1 to 112.4° for the figure’s arrows. Native outline residual 0.915 px mean over 14 frames at our phase; the sweep’s lowest is 0.904 px at -4°. The figure’s column labels were read from its pixels, and each names a frame’s exposure start to the second. The release rotation record reads latitude-first, 0.23° from the published pole.
